title: March Machine Learning Mania 2017, 2nd Place Winner’s Interview: Scott Kellert
why_relevant: Primary-source competition writeup emphasizing heavy feature engineering from pregame information, careful CV, and converting strength estimates into probabilities.
extracted_technique: Opponent-adjusted team quality features; using continuous strength/point-spread style modeling and mapping to probabilities (e.g., via normal CDF / uncertainty) rather than pure classification.
query: March Machine Learning Mania 2017 2nd place winner interview Scott Kellert
takeaway: High leaderboard performance typically comes from leak-free pregame feature engineering (opponent-adjusted team strength) plus a well-designed season-aware validation scheme; probability mapping/calibration is central under Brier-like scoring.

title: How We Calculate NBA Elo Ratings
why_relevant: Provides a concrete, widely-cited Elo probability + margin-of-victory adjustment formula that can be adapted to NCAA regular-season games for strong pre-tourney features.
extracted_technique: Elo win probability mapping via logistic transform; MOV multiplier using (MOV+3)^0.8 divided by (7.5+0.006*elo_diff) to stabilize ratings and reduce autocorrelation.
query: FiveThirtyEight Elo margin of victory multiplier formula 0.8 power 7.5 0.006
takeaway: A MOV-adjusted Elo (and its probability transform) is a strong, cheap signal for matchup prediction; it pairs well with tree models and can be used as a blend component while keeping leakage controlled via day cutoffs.
